Calculate the driving force produced by the engine at $v = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{72000}{12} = 6000\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the entire system ($m_{\text{total}} = 6000\text{ kg}$):
$$F - R_{\text{total}} - m_{\text{total}} g\sin\theta = m_{\text{total}} a$$
$$6000 - (800 + 400) - (6000)(10)(0.06) = 6000a$$
$$6000 - 1200 - 3600 = 6000a \implies 1200 = 6000a \implies a = 0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the trailer alone to find towbar tension $T$:
$$T - R_{\text{trailer}} - m_{\text{trailer}} g\sin\theta = m_{\text{trailer}} a$$
$$T - 400 - (2000)(10)(0.06) = (2000)(0.2)$$
$$T - 1600 = 400 \implies T = 2000\text{ N} \quad (2\text{ kN})$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Evaluate forces on whole combination:
- Driving thrust is $6000\text{ N}$
- Friction is $1200\text{ N}$, gravity is $3600\text{ N}$:
$$a = \frac{6000 - 4800}{6000} = 0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate dynamic towbar tension:
- Trailer drag is $400\text{ N}$ and gravity is $1200\text{ N}$:
$$T = 1600 + 2000(0.2) = 2000\text{ N}$$
The towbar carries $2000\text{ N}$ during acceleration.

Applies Newton's second law to combined system: $a = \frac{6000 - 1200 - 3600}{6000} = 0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Applies equation of motion to trailer: $T - 400 - 2000(10)(0.06) = 2000(0.2)$.
Obtains towbar tension $T = 1600 + 400 = 2000\text{ N}$ (or $2\text{ kN}$).

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 1: Towing vehicle ascending slope with acceleration and terminal tension analysis

hints: At maximum constant speed, acceleration is zero, so $F = 4800\text{ N}$.
Calculate maximum speed: $V = \frac{72000}{4800} = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
For the trailer at steady speed: $T_{\text{steady}} = 400 + 1200 = 1600\text{ N}$.
Calculate the tension ratio: $\frac{1600}{2000} = 0.8$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the terminal velocity up the slope where $a = 0$:
$$F = R_{\text{total}} + m_{\text{total}} g\sin\theta = 4800\text{ N}$$
$$V = \frac{P}{F} = \frac{72000}{4800} = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the towbar tension at this steady speed ($a = 0$):
$$T_{\text{steady}} = R_{\text{trailer}} + m_{\text{trailer}} g\sin\theta = 400 + (2000)(10)(0.06) = 1600\text{ N} \quad (1.6\text{ kN})$$

Compute the ratio of steady-speed tension to accelerating tension:
$$\text{Ratio} = \frac{T_{\text{steady}}}{T_{\text{accel}}} = \frac{1600}{2000} = \frac{4}{5} = 0.8$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find terminal climbing speed:
- With total opposing load $4800\text{ N}$:
$$V = \frac{72000}{4800} = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Evaluate steady towbar tension:
- Without acceleration, tension drops to match static slope load:
$$T_{\text{steady}} = 400 + 1200 = 1600\text{ N}$$

Form tension ratio:
- Tension drops by $20\%$:
$$\frac{1600}{2000} = 0.8$$
The steady tension is $0.8$ times the accelerating tension.

Obtains maximum steady speed $V = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Considers trailer at steady speed: $T_{\text{steady}} = 400 + 1200 = 1600\text{ N}$.
Obtains tension $T_{\text{steady}} = 1600\text{ N}$ and ratio $\frac{1600}{2000} = 0.8$ (or $\frac{4}{5}$).

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Capstone Practice 2: Mountain pass traversal with uphill and downhill power dynamics

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 2: Mountain pass traversal with uphill and downhill power dynamics

hints: Total uphill opposing load is $R + mg\sin\theta = 900 + 1000(10)(0.05) = 900 + 500 = 1400\text{ N}$.
Maximum climbing speed occurs when $a = 0$: $V_1 = \frac{42000}{1400} = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
At $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$, driving force is $F = \frac{42000}{20} = 2100\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law: $a = \frac{2100 - 1400}{1000} = 0.7\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the total opposing force along the climb $AB$:
$$F_{\text{oppose}} = R + mg\sin\theta = 900 + (1000)(10)(0.05) = 900 + 500 = 1400\text{ N}$$

Calculate the maximum steady climbing speed:
$$V_1 = \frac{P}{F_{\text{oppose}}} = \frac{42000}{1400} = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the driving force and acceleration at $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{42000}{20} = 2100\text{ N}$$
$$a = \frac{F - F_{\text{oppose}}}{m} = \frac{2100 - 1400}{1000} = 0.7\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine steady climbing speed:
- Opposing load is $1400\text{ N}$:
$$V_1 = \frac{42000}{1400} = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Find acceleration at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
- Available thrust is $2100\text{ N}$:
$$a = \frac{2100 - 1400}{1000} = 0.7\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The car accelerates at $0.7\text{ m s}^{-2}$ on the climb.

Obtains maximum steady speed up $AB$: $V_1 = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculates driving force at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ ($F = 2100\text{ N}$) and obtains acceleration $a = \frac{2100 - 1400}{1000} = 0.7\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 2: Mountain pass traversal with uphill and downhill power dynamics

hints: At entry to descent ($30\text{ m s}^{-1}$), engine thrust is $F = \frac{42000}{30} = 1400\text{ N}$.
Downhill equation: $F + mg\sin\theta - R = ma \implies 1400 + 500 - 900 = 1000a \implies 1000 = 1000a \implies a = 1\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
At maximum steady speed downhill, acceleration is zero: $F + 500 - 900 = 0 \implies F = 400\text{ N}$.
Calculate terminal descent speed: $V_2 = \frac{42000}{400} = 105\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the driving force at the crest ($v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$):
$$F = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{42000}{30} = 1400\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law down the incline $BC$:
$$F + mg\sin\theta - R = ma$$
$$1400 + (1000)(10)(0.05) - 900 = 1000a$$
$$1400 + 500 - 900 = 1000a \implies 1000 = 1000a \implies a = 1\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Determine the steady maximum speed $V_2$ down $BC$ where $a = 0$:
$$F + mg\sin\theta - R = 0$$
$$F + 500 - 900 = 0 \implies F = 400\text{ N}$$
$$V_2 = \frac{P}{F} = \frac{42000}{400} = 105\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Evaluate initial descent surge:
- Engine thrust is $1400\text{ N}$ plus $500\text{ N}$ downhill gravity:
$$a = \frac{1400 + 500 - 900}{1000} = 1\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate terminal descent speed:
- Steady speed requires engine to supply only the shortfall:
$$F = 900 - 500 = 400\text{ N}$$
$$V_2 = \frac{42000}{400} = 105\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The car can reach a terminal descent speed of $105\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Applies Newton's second law down $BC$: $a = \frac{1400 + 500 - 900}{1000} = 1\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Sets downhill force balance $F + 500 - 900 = 0 \implies F = 400\text{ N}$.
Obtains maximum steady descent speed $V_2 = \frac{42000}{400} = 105\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
